pages.text:
To create an application for general use, you'll need to build a Redirect URI handler to generate access tokens for each of your users. However, if you only want to use the API on your own Gumroad account, you can manually generate an access token, which is a simpler process.

If you're writing some custom code you need to run with your Gumroad account, all you need is an access token. Your access token is used in the request header of every request to the API and should be kept secret, like a password.

Keep the application ID and secret values safe and confidential, but they are not necessary for manually generating an access token. Instead, use the "Generate access token" button to get your access token.

Keep your access token safe and confidential, like a password. When you make an API call, include it in the request's header. Here's an example of a request with the access token (replace ACCESS\_TOKEN with the string from your application):

> curl --request POST \
>
> --url https://api.gumroad.com/oauth/token \
>
> --data code=c302a5e2330ea9a581e370c9c7c9b87760734336ae3253d37e5425a9aa1a04d9 \
>
> --data client\_id=f74e4939f6f9efe74f85ff034af9e9e04540d1e8fce609d652715db5480d4dbe \
>
> --data client\_secret=10173a92c55744b097f0e2a1c4ea03d9dd5b54ad04c82e8efaabbec2d3a8f1f6 \
>
> --data redirect\_uri=https://oauthdebugger.com/debug
>
> {"access\_token":"abf11e4ab2850ffd50ef690257f7a1c998a443059513d1a4826f2b3159620505","token\_type":"Bearer","refresh\_token":"77d7836232246508a6c5b1a9d153d8edbce74249edafaef228554e7be8a29b5e","scope":"edit\_products","created\_at":1609038258}

1. Create an Access Token
2. Make an HTTP call to the Gumroad API
3. Create a Test Membership and Subscribe

Gumroad's documentation for this is very straightforward: . One nice thing Gumroad does is first walk you through access 'For Just Your Gumroad Account'. These are the specific instructions this guide will follow. (other providers start off by walking through the OAuth section, which can be really confusing). At the end of this step you should have a very long string of random characters underneath the box titled 'Access Token'. Hold on to those because you'll need them in Step 2.

1. Change the method from GET to PUT
2. Update the request URL field to   
   https://api.gumroad.com/v2/resource\_subscriptions
3. Add the following three parameters as 'Keys': access\_token, resource\_name, and post\_url.

Last step is to cut and paste your access token from step 1. into the Value section that parameter and enter the URL where you would like to receive this notification in the Value for the post\_url parameter. I used an endpoint on AWS, but if you just wanted to test things you could quickly create an endpoint using something like RequestBin.

Once that was all set up, created a Membership. To do this, I created an incognito browser window and cut and pasted the URL of the product. I'm not sure if that was totally necessary or not, but I figured it'd be good as a matter of practice. Once I subscribed, I went and checked the endpoint I created and, sure enough, the following JSON was posted to that endpoint:

# Quiply API Key: Access to Every Quiply API

One API key that works on every Quiply data API, including every new API we launch. Subscribe once, call them all.

One key for every Quiply API (current and future)

Your API key is the license key Gumroad gives you. It looks like XXXXXXXX-XXXXXXXX-XXXXXXXX-XXXXXXXX. You'll find it in three places: on the confirmation page right after checkout, in your email receipt (click "Get my API key"), and any time later at gumroad.com/library. Your key is active within a minute of purchase.

Send your key in the X-API-Key header on every request, to any Quiply API. Each API's web address, endpoints and copy-paste examples are on its docs page at quiply.net. If you get 401 the key is missing or mistyped, 403 means the subscription is inactive, and 429 means you've reached this month's limit.

## How do you connec

 do you give your assistant?

### What data can it read?

Your products, sales, buyer emails, and payouts, according to the permissions you grant. You can grant some and not others.

### Can it publish products?

New products start as unpublished drafts. With product access, the connector can publish or unpublish them. Review these actions in your MCP client.

### How do customers buy?

Share your product’s Gumroad link. Customers pay through Gumroad checkout. The MCP server does not take payments in your chat.

### How do I revoke access?

Revoke the connection any time in Settings > Applications. Disconnecting the connector in your chat app does not revoke its access token, so revoke it here to end the connection.

Let an MCP-compatible AI client search Jira, summarize sprints and report on projects. If you choose, it can also file bugs, update issues, comment and move tickets through your workflow. This bundle gives you the working code and the explanation of why it is built the way it is.

You research apps for an agent-toolkit builder. App: Gumroad (category: Ecommerce; hint: gumroad.com/api).
Using ONLY the SOURCES below, fill the schema. Rules:
- access: can a developer get credentials themselves for free (self_serve_free), only on a paid plan/trial, only after app review/approval, or only via partnership/contact sales?
- buildability: could this be an agent toolkit today (yes / yes_with_caveats / no); blocker = main obstacle, else "none".
- existing_mcp only if SOURCES show it; otherwise none_found (or unknown if sources are silent).
- evidence: for each of auth_methods, access, api_types, existing_mcp give a url from SOURCES and a SHORT VERBATIM quote (<=200 chars) copied exactly from that source's text. No quote available -> say unknown, do not invent.
- If sources are insufficient, use "unknown". Never guess from memory.
